## Review posture

The baseline is empty, so every `churn`, `recency`, `blast_radius` and `blast_radius_importers` score is `0` **by construction** — not because the code is safe. That leaves three usable axes: `severity`, `confidence`, and `agent_risk`. I'm ranking on those, and I'm treating `agent_risk` as an independent blocking reason, not a tiebreaker — a medium-severity finding that will mislead the next agent editing this code can block where a high-severity cosmetic finding does not.

Totals: **37 findings — 8 block, 19 warn, 10 ignore.** Plus 1 suppressed finding (`suppressed_count: 1`, the gap at `crime_00021`) that a reviewer should re-check, since suppressions inherited into a fresh PR have no baseline to justify them.

---

## 🛑 Block merge (8)

| ID | Charge | sev | agent_risk | Why it blocks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crime_00017` | Localhost-on-Disk `src/api/files.ts:9` | 0.6 med | 0.30 | `/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/schema.json` at confidence 0.90. This is not a risk, it's a defect: the path exists on exactly one laptop. CI and every other dev break on first run. Low agent_risk is irrelevant — deterministic breakage. |
| `crime_00016` | Dev-Server URL `src/api/files.ts:8` | 0.6 med | 0.30 | Same file, same class. `localhost:3000` hardcoded in non-config source, confidence 0.90. Ships a build that can only talk to one machine's dev server. |
| `crime_00010` | Half-UTC, Half-Local `src/date.ts` | **0.8 high** | 0.36 | One receiver reads `getUTCFullYear()` @L9 and `getMonth()` @L41. Silently wrong by the host's UTC offset, and wrong *only* off-UTC — so it passes on the author's machine and corrupts billing dates in production. High severity + 0.85 confidence. |
| `crime_00012` | Timezone Roulette `src/date.ts:29,33` | 0.6 med | 0.35 | Blocking as part of the same defect, not on its own weight: `"2026-12-25T07:00:00"` and `"2026-12-20"` parse against the runtime's zone. Fixing `crime_00010` without this leaves the module half-correct. |
| `crime_00001` | Temporal Recklessness `src/date.ts` | **0.8 high** | **0.44** | Highest `agent_risk` in the report. 8 clock reads across the domain date module with `test_gap: 0.5` — nothing can pin a fixed moment, so the two bugs above are untestable and un-regressable. Blocking the clock injection is what makes the other two fixes verifiable. |
| `crime_00015` | False Identity `calculateRefundPreview` | 0.55 med | 0.31 | The clearest agent-risk block. A `calculate*Preview` name that calls `saveRefundAudit` and `sendRefundEmail`. Only medium severity — but any agent or human treating it as pure (which the name invites) emails a customer about a refund that was never issued. Severity understates this; agent_risk is the reason it blocks. |
| `crime_00005` | God Function `generateInvoice` (204 lines) | **0.9 high** | 0.38 | Highest severity in the report, 0.95 confidence, 3.4× threshold, `test_gap: 0` — and this is *new* code. Extraction costs minutes now and never gets cheaper. Blocking a 204-line invoice orchestrator is standard for new-code review. |
| `crime_00025` | Test That Proves Nothing `src/billing.test.ts:4-6` | 0.45 med | 0.27 | Zero `expect`/`assert` calls, 0.88 confidence. The PR introduces a whole billing subsystem behind two tests, one of which asserts nothing. Merging it records green coverage that protects no behaviour — a false-confidence signal for every future agent edit. |

The three `src/date.ts` items (`00001`, `00010`, `00012`) are one blocking comment, not three: *fix the time handling and make it testable.*

---

| `crime_00019` | Concept Alias Drift (tenant) | 0.55 | 0.30 | `account`/`organisation`/`team`/`workspace` across 5 files. Naming decision, not a defect — needs a human call on the canonical term. |

## ✅ Ignore (10)

Not "wrong" — just below the bar for comment on this PR. All have `agent_risk ≤ 0.29` and `severity ≤ 0.35`.

| ID | Charge | sev | agent_risk | Why ignore |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crime_00023` | Temporal Recklessness `state.ts:18` | 0.35 | 0.28 | One `Date.now()`. Falls out of the blocked clock-injection work for free. |
| `crime_00026` | Date String Sewing `date.ts:41` | 0.3 | 0.26 | Inside a file being rewritten anyway. |
| `crime_00027` | Host-Locale Drift `date.ts:46` | 0.3 | 0.26 | Same — one `toLocaleDateString()`, will be swept up. |
| `crime_00009` | Option Bag Junk Drawer | 0.3 | 0.38 | agent_risk is respectable, but confidence 0.74 and it's a taste call on a 10-line function. Not review-worthy at this size. |
| `crime_00011` | Negative Flag Maze | 0.25 | 0.36 | One `!a && !b`. Genuinely readable as written. |
| `crime_00022` / `crime_00028` | Unprefixed Boolean ×2 | 0.3 | 0.29 / 0.26 | `paid`/`expired`/`stale`/`disableBilling`/`skipRetry` — house-style, belongs in lint config, not PR review. |
| `crime_00024` | Plural Mismatch | 0.3 | 0.28 | Detector self-declares "v1 — type aliases and generics silently skipped", confidence 0.70. Too weak to spend review attention on. |
| `crime_00036` | Icon-Sized Raster (32×32 PNG) | 0.35 | 0.16 | Preference, not a defect. |
| `crime_00038` | Unfinished Business `billing.ts` | 0.2 | **0.08** | Lowest aggregate in the report — 4 markers at 12.9/1k LOC, barely over a threshold of 10. Correctly ranked last; ignore. |

---

## The call

**Request changes.** Two of the eight blockers (`crime_00016`, `crime_00017`) are certain breakage outside the author's machine and would fail CI on a real pipeline. Three more are a single coherent ask — make `src/date.ts` deterministic and timezone-correct. The remaining three are the new-code standard: don't merge a 204-line orchestrator, a `calculate*` that emails customers, or a billing test with no assertions.

The two findings I'd defend hardest against a "just fix the highs" reading: **`crime_00015` blocks at medium severity** because its agent_risk is the whole point — the name lies about side effects — and **`crime_00032` warns at high severity** because a 592-byte SVG with an embedded raster is not worth a merge gate. Ranking on severity alone gets both of these backwards.
